summary: Sonam Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko in 1960 and held a post as Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Sonam Kachru works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~2008–2015) under Dan Arnold. He held positions at the University of Virginia (2015), Forum Transregionale Studien, and the Max Planck Institute.

Sonam Thakchoe works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and held a post at the University of Tasmania around 2006.

Sonam Tsering specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Columbia University (~2012–2021) under doctoral supervisor Gray Tuttle, having also studied under numerous teachers including Khenzur Dawa, Janet Gyatso, and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Songeun Choe studied history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe completed an MA at Dongguk University under Myung-dae Moon and earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1991 under Kiyohiko Munakata.

Sonja Arntzen is a Japanologist. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1979), completing her doctorate under Leon Hurvitz in 1979, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonya S. Lee specializes in art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (~1998–2004) under Wu Hung, taught at Swarthmore College, and joined the University of Southern California around 2005.

Soon-il Hwang works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seungwon Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford (~1998–2003) under Richard Gombrich, later taking a post at Dongguk University around 2003.
Soorakkulame Pemarathana works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the National University of Singapore (~2002–2004) under the supervision of Saranindranath Tagore.
Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held an academic post at Uppsala University.
Soshuku Shibatani specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1974–1979) and held a post as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University.

Souleymane Bachir Diagne is a philosopher educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Harvard, École Normale Supérieure, and Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne. He held academic posts at Université Cheikh Anta Diop (~1982–2002), Northwestern University (~2002–2007), and Columbia University (from ~2008).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of Houston, the University of North Carolina Wilmington (~2018–2021), and Harvard University (~2021).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD 1964–1966), and served as Professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1968–1997).

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, sinology, and history. She earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2004–2006) and a PhD at Columbia University (~2008–2015), where she later held a post.

Stanislas Julien was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France (~1823–1827), where he subsequently served as Professor of Chinese language and literature and Administrator from 1832 to 1873.

Stanley Insler was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Columbia College, the University of Tübingen, and Yale University, he held a faculty post at Yale University from ~1964 to 2015.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Ceylon, Cornell University, and Harvard University, he held posts at the University of Cambridge (~1963–1972) and Harvard University (~1976–2001).

Stanley Weinstein specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Harvard University and served as a professor at the University of London (~1962–1968) and Yale University (~1968–1999).

Stanley Wolpert was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, and served as a professor of history at the University of California, Los Angeles from ~1959 to 2002.
